1:b2|# TASK
2:7c|The project (doc, checked out at an old commit) has this issue:
3:00|
4:70|Instance variables link to other variables of the same name in the project
5:55|**Describe the bug**
6:17|Assume autodoc is used via apidoc. In theory other combinations of autodoc (or maybe even without it) can cause this to occur, but this would be the most common occurrence.
7:00|
8:ad|If a global variable (or really, any kind of variable, just that this would be the most common occurrence) exists, and inside a class you decide to document a variable of the same name, the document of the instance variable will link to the other occurence of a variable under the same name.
9:00|
10:6c|This can even occur across subpackages and even across other classes of those subpackages (although this appears to occur less often and seemingly...randomly? This only occurs sometimes (presumably due to the referencing heuristic?)).
11:00|
12:6e|This is a problem, because, for example, `somepackage.subA::Foo.somename` could be and usually is completely unrelated to  `somepackage.subB::Bar.somename`. Furthermore, `somepackage::Foo.somename` (instance variable) could be completely unrelated to `somepackage.somename` (global variable). Of course this latter example is far less likely, but the *auto*linking of these two together, is strange.
13:00|
14:57|**To Reproduce**
15:48|Steps to reproduce the behavior:
16:cd|```
17:c6|$ git clone https://github.com/13steinj/sphinx-issue-examples/
18:a2|$ cd sphinx-issue-examples
19:ce|$ git checkout referenced_variables
20:cc|$ cd docs
21:b4|$ make html
22:c8|$ cd _build/html && python -m SimpleHTTPServer 8008
23:cd|```
24:b7|then open 127.0.0.1:8008 in a browser
25:00|
26:fc|**Expected behavior**
27:63|That the class variable documentation not be linked to any other. It is unreasonable to expect these to be in any way related whatsoever. If they *happen* to be, the user can decide to document it as such with a simple reference to the other variable, such as "see :const:\`somename\`".
28:00|
29:b0|There is no reason that a `limit` variable on some class of some database-oriented subpackage autolink to the `limit` variable on some class of some config-related subpackage (this is what occurred in my codebase, which is private at least while in development. I cannot provide anything except a heavily censored screenshot, as I do not know of a way to trick the referencing heuristic to cause a link to occur in an demo repo).
30:00|
31:96|**Your project**
32:2a|https://github.com/13steinj/sphinx-issue-examples/tree/referenced_variables
33:00|
34:2e|**Screenshots**
35:d4|Not really applicable because this is example independent but here you go anyway:
36:01|![image](https://user-images.githubuser
37:00|
38:ab|Find the cause and make the minimal correct fix in the source (not in tests).
39:07|Do NOT modify or add tests. Do NOT commit. Leave your changes in the working tree.

reasoning_content:
This is the Sphinx project. The issue is about instance variables linking to other variables of the same name. This is a known Sphinx issue (#7392? or similar). Let me think — the fix is in `sphinx/domains/python.py`, in the `PythonDomain.resolve_xref` or `find_obj` — the heuristic that when resolving a reference for an attribute, it searches for objects with the same name in other classes.

Actually, this is Sphinx issue #7392 "Instance variables link to other variables of the same name in the project". The fix was in `sphinx/domains/python.py` — `find_obj` — the fuzzy search: when a reference like `somename` is resolved, it searches `objtypes for modname` etc. Let me recall the actual fix.

The actual upstream fix: PR #7393? Let me think. The issue is that in `PythonDomain.resolve_xref`, when autodoc documents an instance variable (attribute), the refct is like `:py:attr:`somename`` with no explicit target, and the resolution heuristic searches for any object named `somename` in the current module, then in the whole project.

reasoning_content:
Interesting: the module-level global `somename = "global-in-subA"` did NOT get registered as an object (no `OBJ: somepackage.subA.somename`) because autodoc's `:members:` only documents members with docstrings... module-level variables need `#:` comments or docstrings to be documented. The global wasn't documented, so no `py:obj` target for bare `somename`... but wait — the `:ivar:` field xref with reftarget='somename', py:class='Foo', py:module='somepackage.subA' in refspecific mode: find_obj searchmode==1: fullname = 'somepackage.subA.Foo.somename' exists → newname = that. So the link goes to the class's own attribute — correct behavior, no bug shown.

To show the bug I need the case where the class attribute is NOT documented as py:attribute (so fullname doesn't exist) but a same-named variable IS documented somewhere. E.g.:
- subA: module-level `#: doc\nsomename = "global"` → documented as py:data 'somepackage.subA.somename'? Actually with automodule :members:, module-level vars with `#:` comments get documented as py:data with fullname 'somepackage.subA.somename'.
- class Foo with `:ivar somename:` docstring field, but no `#:`-documented attribute.

Then the :ivar xref (reftarget='somename', py:class='Foo', py:module='somepackage.subA', refspecific): searchmode==1: fullname 'somepackage.subA.Foo.somename' NOT in objects → modname+'.'+name = 'somepackage.subA.somename' IS in objects (the global) → links to the global. That's the bug: :ivar somename links to the module global (or worse, fuzzy-matches into another subpackage's attribute).

Even better cross-package case: subB has class Bar with `:ivar somename:` and nothing named somename in subB; subA has documented global or attribute somename. Then fuzzy search finds 'somepackage.subA.Foo.somename' or 'somepackage.subA.somename' → Bar's :ivar links into subA. That's exactly the issue's complaint.

Note: the fix (dropping rolename='obj') removes the xref entirely for :var:/:ivar:/:cvar: fields — so no link at all. That's the upstream-accepted behavior.
